old_title: Iran war live: Tehran threatens to prolong war until Trump's term ends
new_title: Trump says Strait of Hormuz will soon be 'called a territory of the US': Live
old_text:
Iran has suggested it could deliberately prolong the war with the US until Donald Trump leaves office, in order to send a message that attacking the country has lasting consequences.
Mohammad Reza Naghdi, senior adviser to the commander of Iran's Revolutionary Guards, said dragging out the war would show any future US administration that "there is a cost" to hostile endeavours against Iran.
"We have to attain deterrence so that the enemy never dares to attack us, so we can live with security," he told PBS NewsHour.
His comments came as Iran again rejected Donald Trump's claims that the US has "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority said "the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked" and it will not be opened until Iran's conditions are accepted.
Trump earlier said that "praise be to Allah", Washington has "total control over the Strait of Hormuz", adding: "I THINK WE WILL KEEP IT!"
Amid their conflicting claims, data from trade intelligence firm Kpler showed shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz was near a three-month low.
Just 13 vessels transited the waterway on Tuesday, around 90 per cent below the pre-war daily average.
Jared Kushner to head to Middle East for Gaza talks
President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner will travel to the Middle East next week to try to advance plans for an end to the conflict in Gaza after a deal recently announced by the Trump administration ran into Israeli opposition.
An official with the Board of Peace, the body Trump established to oversee the fragile ceasefire in the Israel-Hamas war, said Kushner, board high representative Nickolay Mladenov, and executive board member Tony Blair would arrive in Israel on Sunday.
The group will then travel to Cairo, where meetings of a Palestinian technocratic group set to assume control of Gaza under a US-brokered ceasefire deal have been taking place for the past several months.
Iran and Oman work to clean oil spills from attacked ships
Iran said it was working to clean up an oil spill off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Images distributed by Iran's semiofficial news agency ISNA showed oil fouling the island's beaches.
While Iran hasn't said what caused the spill, the firm TankerTrackers.com says it appears to have started with an Iranian attack on a bulk carrier off Oman.
Oman is responding to another spill in the Arabian Sea, coming from a tanker grounded off its southern coast. The tanker Caroline Bezengi, a sanctioned vessel believed to be part of Russia's "shadow fleet", has been grounded since reporting an explosion in June.
A British maritime risk and response company, which has been hired to salvage the tanker, said oil from the ship has reached shores hundreds of km north of the vessel.

Vance says Iran war will end with US in stronger position
Vice president JD Vance appeared to be lowering expectations for the Strait of Hormuz to return to the way it was before the war.
He predicted in an interview on Fox News that the war will end with the US in a stronger position, with Iran not having a nuclear weapon, and with the Strait of Hormuz "returned to a place where oil and gas prices are stable for the American people".
"That's goal number one: keep oil and gas cheap for Americans all over our country," he said.
The second goal, according to Vance, is to ensure that Iran will never get a nuclear weapon.
Oil steadies after US threatens indefinite blockade
Oil prices inched up this morning after the US threatened an indefinite naval blockade of Iran, reviving concerns about supply of crude after the previous session's fall on a weaker outlook for demand and a large build in US stocks.
Brent futures rose 1 cent, or 0.1 per cent, to $87.08 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose 6 cents to $81.31 a barrel.
Yesterday, the US warned that it could maintain a naval blockade of Iran indefinitely and ramp up economic pressure on Tehran as ceasefire talks have stalled.

Crew of Yemeni vessel recount their chaotic rescue after Houthis' deadly attack
Crew members of a Yemeni commercial ship who survived a deadly attack by Houthi rebels earlier this week said a second missile struck the vessel just as rescue efforts from the initial strike were underway, causing even more chaos and casualties.
In all, three ballistic missiles fired by the Iran-backed Houthis struck the ship in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, just off Yemen's coast, as it was coming into port, killing six people and injuring at least nine others, according to Yemeni authorities.
It was part of an escalating campaign by the Houthis and their first deadly attack this year on a vessel navigating the strait, which connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and accounts for roughly 12 per cent of global trade.
"People were burning ... it was a strange scene of doomsday," said Zaheer Ahmed, a Pakistani crew member recovering at a hospital in the port city of Mokha.
"I shouted for help and a Yemeni soldier came to my aid," said Ahmed, who was injured in both legs.
All three of the crew members The Associated Press interviewed at the hospital described intense fire, panic and damage aboard the ship, which was struck before dawn on Tuesday.
US official says it would be 'wise' for Iran to agree to peace deal
A US official has said it would be "wise" for Iran to agree to a peace deal as the war in the Middle East drags on.
While Donald Trump "has been consistent in saying he prefers a diplomatic solution, he continues to retain all options if Iran continues to engage in terrorism and refuses to make a deal", the official told NewsNations.
"The successful sanctions and blockade have crippled Iran's economy and left Iran in an extremely degraded state. It would be wise for Iran to agree to a deal - otherwise, they know what will happen".
US military denies reports of sailor deaths and suicidal ideation on the USS Abraham Lincoln
US Central Command had denied reports that seven sailors died in a brawl aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln in the Middle East and that there had been a spike in suicidal ideation on the aircraft carrier.
"USS Abraham Lincoln has maintained among the highest crew reenlistment rates (84.4%) of all aircraft carriers in the U.S. Navy", CENTCOM wrote on X.
"No service members aboard the aircraft carrier have died, and the one Sailor who fell overboard Aug. 3 was quickly and safely recovered. The rampant misreporting on Abraham Lincoln's historic deployment is a disservice to our men and women in uniform and their loved ones".
Top US Democrat calls reports of deteriorating conditions on USS Abraham Lincoln a 'disgrace'
A top US Democrat has called reports of deteriorating conditions on USS Abraham Lincoln in the Middle East a "disgrace".
"Food shortages. Rationing. Mental Health Challenges. Lack of fresh fruits and vegetables", Hakeem Jeffries, the minority leader for the House of Representatives, wrote on X. "Republicans need to end their reckless war of choice in Iran immediately".
new_text:
Donald Trump has said he will soon declare the Strait of Hormuz a US territory.
The US president escalated his rhetoric over the vital waterway that carries a significant share of global oil supplies, as he spoke to the media on Friday.
He also told Fox News that the US will hit Iran hard economically as Washington and Tehran struggle to reach a deal to end a nearly six-month conflict.
His comments come as the US prepares to deploy the USS George Washington to the Middle East to relieve military personnel stationed on the USS Abraham Lincoln for more than 200 days amid growing concerns about living conditions on the aircraft carrier, according to reports.
The Lincoln has been deployed for more than 250 days and has not made a port call in 200 days, setting a record for consecutive days at sea, according to US senator Richard Blumenthal, who wrote to Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth about concerns for those on board.
Blumenthal cited reports of "shortages of basic supplies, water contamination, plumbing issues, deteriorating mental health, deck safety concerns, and disruptions in the mail system".
Trump officials have dismissed concerns about the conditions of the USS Lincoln.
US seeking mediation from more European countries - report
The Trump administration appears to be seeking support from more countries to help pressure Iran to stop the war, reports suggest.
Earlier this week, US secretary of state Marco Rubio met with the foreign minister of Austria in Washington and held a call with the foreign minister of Greece, AP News reported.
While official readouts of the discussions did not mention Iran by name, both foreign ministers reportedly spoke with Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi later in the week.
The diplomatic move comes as both the US and Iran are pushing for control of the Strait of Hormuz, and negotiations between countries including Pakistan and Oman with Iran have progressed at an uneven pace.

ICYMI: US military loses 25% of its key drone fleet as Iran war shrinks stockpile: report
Donald Trump's Iran war has reportedly cost the US military about one-quarter of the drones that a top general recently likened to "the most valuable player" in America's weapons lineup.
At least 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones have been shot down or crashed, leaving no more than 145 remaining in dwindling defense stockpiles, The Washington Post said Tuesday, citing three unidentified officials familiar with the matter.
Each drone costs from $30 million to $50 million, depending on its sensors and missiles, which puts the loss to taxpayers at more than $1.3 billion, the Post said.

Israeli officials shocked by the speed of Iran's military recovery after war, report says
Israeli military and intelligence officials were stunned by the rate of Iran's military recovery after the first weeks of the 2026 war, according to a report.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the Israel Defense Forces was taken aback by how fast the Islamic Republic was able to reconstitute its forces after the main phase of fighting, including the redevelopment of its ballistic missile threat.

Poll: Just 29% of expected midterm voters say they approve of Trump's handling of Iran
A cable TV polling expert claims that numbers from two surveys conducted two years apart show just how deeply US President Donald Trump has disappointed America's voters when it comes to Iran.
CNN chief data analyst Harry Enten said Tuesday that a July 2024 poll of people who were extremely motivated to vote in that year's presidential election found that 53 percent were confident Trump would be able to handle the situation in Iran, according to a video clip posted online.
But a July poll of people extremely motivated to vote in November's midterm elections shows that just 29 percent now approve of how Trump is actually handling Iran, Enten said.
"We're talking about a 24-point fall in just two years", he said. "What was an advantage for President Trump going into the 2024 election amongst those who really wanted to turn out and vote has turned into a tremendous disadvantage this time around".
Read on...
Father of USS Lincoln sailor said he's heard 'positive feedback,' but admits mental toll
The father of a sailor aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln has said he's heard "pretty positive feedback" about the aircraft carrier's conditions, but admits to the mental toll deployment has taken on the service members.
"As far as my particular child, I've heard pretty positive feedback about the conditions there", he told CNN. "And we understand that they're under a lot of mental stress and have nothing but sympathy and respect for the hardships and the stress that are inherent to the operation".
It follows reports of poor maintenance, food supply issues and sailors struggling with their mental health on the aircraft carrier deployed to the Middle East for more than 200 days.
Watch: Trump refutes military family concerns as conditions deteriorate on board USS Abraham Lincoln
Israeli officials shocked by the speed of Iran's military recovery after war, report says
Israeli military and intelligence officials were stunned by the rate of Iran's military recovery after the first weeks of the 2026 war, according to a report.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) was taken aback by how fast the Islamic Republic was able to reconstitute its forces after the main phase of fighting, including the redevelopment of its ballistic missile threat.
Iran launched missiles at Israel at the beginning of June and rose to an escalation in early July with renewed strikes on Arab states in the region. They were also accused of striking ships in the Strait of Hormuz, maintaining a hold over the vital waterway.
In full:
Trump says he will declare Strait of Hormuz US territory
Donald Trump has said that he will declare the Strait of Hormuz a US territory.
"After we finish defeating Iran, which is being very badly defeated, pretty soon I'll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States", Trump said to cheers at an event in New York Friday.
Washington and Tehran both claim to have control over the vital oil waterway, which has been effectively closed amid the war.
